key_insights.title: Mechanism
key_insights.body: large 3D channels fully occupied by an identical translational net → porosity

key_insights.title: Design Rule
key_insights.body: [positive] control dihedral angles when assembling networks from square-planar nodes → enables assembly of a specific network based solely on square-planar nodes instead of the usually favored 2D 4^4 grid

key_insights.title: Design Rule
key_insights.body: [positive] apply a one-pot copper-mediated hydrothermal reaction of nitriles and ammonia → gives a novel, non-hydrazine synthetic route to 3,5-disubstituted 1,2,4-triazoles

key_insights.title: Failure
key_insights.body: [performance_regression] self-assemble square-planar building blocks into extended structures without controlling dihedral angles: 2D square grids (4^4) are favored instead of the desired 3D network based solely on square-planar nodes

notable_quotes: Using Cu(OH)2 or Cu2(OH)2CO3 with ammonia and nitriles gave [Cu(mtz)]n or [Cu(ptz)]n in moderate yields up to 40%.
Compound 1 has an unprecedented 4.8.16 topology with 1D CuI–triazolate helices and large 3D channels occupied by an interpenetrating net.
The triazolate ligands likely form by coupling nitriles with ammonia, while CuII may act as an oxidant to assist proton elimination in cycloaddition.
